$comment: BMW 3 Series E46 (330i/330Ci and M3) with a GM LS1 or LS3: the hardware real builds use, researched 2026-09-29 from vendor product pages (Sikky Manufacturing, TDR Performance, Pennsyltucky Performance, Vorshlag Motorsports, Wiring Specialties, PMC Motorsport via its own shop and PO Performance, Rank One Performance); every page cited is saved and quote-checked. Prices as listed on 2026-09-29, in the currency printed. Covered: engine and transmission mounts (T56, T56 Magnum, TR6060, CD009, and the car's own ZF/Getrag), the Sikky pan, headers, steering shafts and lines, heater hoses, header-clearance chassis parts, LS-to-BMW gearbox adapters (the M3 Getrag 420G and the 330i ZF boxes), car-specific harnesses, Haltech Rebel ECU packages and CAN-bus cluster modules. Generic LS hardware (GM PCMs, T56/TR6060, clutches, universal pans, LS-to-CD009 adapters) is in the common LS file. Not found: an E46 LS driveshaft listing, an E46 LS radiator, any factory GM pan named as clearing the E46, whether the M3 needs different engine mounts, whether DSC still works, and the ZF boxes' torque ratings. Dirty Dingo lists no E46 in its by-model index; CX Racing blocks automated reading and is not included. Merged 2026-09-29 with the hardware common to every LS swap (GM PCM, Chevrolet Performance and Holley ECU routes, standalone harnesses, GM and Tremec gearboxes, clutches, fuel regulators), which a separate research pass sourced; those parts repeat in each LS swap file until Phase 3 moves them into parts/.

notes: M3 vs 330i: the sources show three differences: M3-specific lower control-arm bushings for header clearance (Sikky CA-Bushing3), M3 and SMG options in the Wiring Specialties harnesses and CAN modules, and the gearbox route (the M3 Getrag 420G takes the PMC Getrag 420 kit or Rank One kit, which use an M3 clutch; the 330i ZF boxes take the PMC plate with a flywheel to suit). No source says whether the engine mounts or subframe differ. Gearbox routes: T56 or T56 Magnum (Sikky CM44, Vorshlag, Pennsyltucky), TR6060 (Sikky CM45, Pennsyltucky), Nissan CD009 (Sikky CM44 with TM03, Pennsyltucky), or the car's own ZF/Getrag with an adapter and the Pennsyltucky adjustable crossmember. Most mounts and headers are LHD-only. CAN: Wiring Specialties harnesses and RevCAN2 modules drive the tach, gauges and lamps; the tach needs a Dakota Digital SGi-8 with a V8.
